# Maintainers

Maintainers are trusted contributors responsible for the health, safety, and
direction of Git Submodule Manager.

## Current Maintainers

| Maintainer | GitHub | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Martin Calander | [@martincalander](https://github.com/martincalander) | Project lead and release maintainer |

Ownership rules are recorded in [CODEOWNERS](CODEOWNERS). Authorship and
attribution are recorded separately in [AUTHORS.md](../AUTHORS.md) and
[NOTICE.md](../NOTICE.md).

## Responsibilities

Maintainers are expected to:

- put stability, repository safety, and cross-platform compatibility first;
- review pull requests and request tests for meaningful failure cases;
- triage issues without promising timelines that cannot be met;
- keep credentials, private reports, and embargoed vulnerabilities private;
- maintain accurate package metadata, documentation, CI, and release notes;
- follow the [governance](GOVERNANCE.md),
  [security policy](SECURITY.md), and [release process](RELEASING.md);
- disclose conflicts of interest that could affect a project decision.

Maintainers may close reports or proposals that are unsafe, unsupported,
duplicate, unactionable, or outside the project's documented scope. Whenever
practical, the reason should be stated clearly.

## Becoming a Maintainer

Martin Calander appoints maintainers after sustained contributions demonstrate
sound technical judgment, reliable follow-through, cross-platform awareness,
and careful handling of Git, Unity, and security failures. There is no commit
quota. Repository permissions are granted gradually and remain no broader than
necessary.

## Inactivity and Removal

A maintainer may step down at any time. The project lead may reduce or remove
access that is no longer needed, including after prolonged inactivity or for
security, conduct, or trust reasons. Before leaving, a maintainer should hand
off open security reports, release work, and any access that only they control.
